text.p: French state-controlled insurance group GAN, which the government plans to privatise, said on Wednesday it had launched the sale of its property financing unit UIC which holds a large portfolio of real estate assets and loans.
The sale is part of GAN's restructuring, the insurer said in a statement.
It also said that it and its insurance units were selling 86 percent of Union pour le Financement d'Immeulbles de Societes (UIS) in a move to maximise their value.
The French government announced a 20 billion franc rescue package earlier this year for GAN as part of a cleanup of the group of which some seven billion francs was earmarked to cover losses at UIC.
A number of so-called vulture investment funds are expected to be interested in UIC's property and loan portfolio.
UIC ran up 30 billion francs of losses in three years and has been at the main root of of GAN's financial problems.
A host of insurance companies have said they are interested in GAN, including French rival AGF and Allianz of Germany.
France's new Socialist government said last week that it would go ahead with its conservative predecessors' plans to privatise GAN.
